title: Unemployment Insurance Appeals: Filing Terms by Docket
content:
**Terms of filing an appeal — Unemployment Insurance Appeals.** An appeal is filed in writing, through the online portal, by mail or by fax, and no fee is charged. The deadline for filing is a number of calendar days counted from a mailing date, and the date that counts as the filing date is the postmark, fax or online submission date. Each party may have one appeal at a time against the same determination or decision. An appeal filed after the deadline may still proceed on a finding of good cause, but never once the late-appeal limit — a number of calendar days after the filing deadline — has passed. The appellant is mailed an acknowledgment with the docket number within a number of business days after filing.

## Terms by docket

| Docket | Filing deadline (calendar days) | Deadline counted from | Late-appeal limit (calendar days after the deadline) | Acknowledgment mailed within (business days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lower Authority Appeal — Separation Issue | 21 | mailing date of the determination | 180 | 5 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Able and Available Issue | 21 | mailing date of the determination | 180 | 5 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination | 21 | mailing date of the determination | 180 | 5 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Overpayment and Fraud | 30 | mailing date of the determination | 180 | 5 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Benefit Charge | 30 | mailing date of the determination | 90 | 5 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Contribution Rate | 30 | mailing date of the determination | 90 | 5 |
| Higher Authority Appeal — Board of Review | 21 | mailing date of the lower-authority decision | 90 | 5 |

## Terms common to every docket

| Term | All seven dockets |
|---|---|
| Date that counts as the filing date | the postmark, fax or online submission date |
| Channels (an appeal must be in writing) | online portal; mail; fax |
| Filing fee | $0 (no fee) |
| Appeals one party may have open against the same determination or decision | 1 |
| Late appeal may proceed on a finding of good cause | yes |

## Points of reading

- The deadline and the late-appeal limit are two different spans: the first is counted from the mailing date, the second from the end of the deadline. On the Separation Issue docket, for example, the deadline is 21 calendar days after the determination's mailing date and the late-appeal limit runs a further 180 calendar days after that deadline.
- Within the late-appeal limit, a late appeal proceeds only on a finding of good cause; beyond the limit it is never accepted, whatever the reason.
- A Board of Review appeal counts its 21 days from the mailing date of the lower-authority decision, not from the original determination.
